expr: (list (progn (string-match "foo" "Foo bar") (replace-match "baz" nil t "Foo bar")) (progn (string-match "foo" "FOO bar") (replace-match "baz" nil t "FOO bar")) (progn (string-match "foo" "FOO bar") (replace-match "baz" t t "FOO bar")))
note: FIXEDCASE, both ways round, on the two cases the argument exists for. Emacs answers ("Baz bar" "BAZ bar" "baz bar"): with FIXEDCASE nil a capitalised match capitalises the replacement and an upcased match upcases it, and with FIXEDCASE t the replacement goes in verbatim. The subject strings are chosen so the MATCH ITSELF is already in the string -- kg folds no case, so a pattern that needed folding to match would be measuring a different divergence (phase15-replace-regexp-case is that one). kg answers `void-function'. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION: kg's own `replace-regexp-in-string' accepts FIXEDCASE and IGNORES it (doc/lisp-api.md), so a `replace-match' that honours it makes the two names disagree about the same argument -- a decision 26.2 owes an answer, of the kind Phase 25.2 had to give for `string=' against `string<'.
